cards.text: Jesus is still giving John letters for seven churches, and John is writing them down (Revelation 1:11, 17-19). This one goes to the angel of the church in Pergamum, from the One who holds the sharp, double-edged sword. Friend, the only letter I ever wrote was on the back of a takeout menu, and it did NOT open like that.
First, Jesus says He knows where they live. And friend, it is NOT the kind of neighborhood you brag about in the group chat.

cards.question: What does Jesus say sits right there in Pergamum?
Living right where Satan's throne sits, the church in Pergamum has denied its faith in Jesus.

cards.text: They held on even in the days of a man Jesus calls "My faithful witness Antipas." Jesus knows his name. Let that sit for a second.

cards.question: What happened to Antipas, Jesus' faithful witness, in Pergamum?

answers.text: He was driven out of town

cards.text: Uh oh, here comes the turn. Jesus has a few things against them, because some of them hold to the teaching of Balaam, a prophet that Balak, king of Moab, once hired to curse Israel (Numbers 22:4-6).

cards.question: Jesus says Balaam taught Balak to place a stumbling block before the Israelites. What was it meant to lead them into?

answers.text: Worship of the sun and moon

cards.question: Balaam's teaching is the only wrong teaching Jesus calls out in Pergamum.

cards.text: Some of them also hold to the teaching of the Nicolaitans, the same group Ephesus got credit for hating (Revelation 2:6). Friend, I once burned two batches in one morning, and the smoke alarm stopped calling it an accident.

cards.question: So what does Jesus tell Pergamum to do? One word: ___!
If Pergamum doesn't repent, Jesus says He'll come shortly and wage war. With what?

cards.text: Then the line every letter has had so far: "He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches." I checked, friend. That means you.

cards.question: Jesus makes a promise to the one who overcomes in Pergamum, and it starts with food. What is it?

answers.text: Fruit from the tree of life

cards.question: Jesus also promises the one who overcomes a white stone with a new ___ written on it.
The new name on the white stone is known to everyone in the church.

cards.text: Next letter goes to the angel of the church in Thyatira. This time Jesus calls Himself the Son of God, whose eyes are like a blazing fire and whose feet are like polished bronze.

cards.question: Jesus knows Thyatira's love, faith, service and perseverance. How do their latest deeds compare to their first?

answers.text: Not as good as at first

cards.text: And you knew it was coming, friend: Jesus has something against them. They tolerate a woman He calls Jezebel, and she calls herself a prophetess.

cards.question: Jezebel's teaching misleads Jesus' servants into the same two sins Balaam's teaching did in Pergamum.

cards.text: Jesus says He gave her time to repent of her immorality. Friend, the snooze button gives me nine extra minutes and I use EVERY single one.

cards.question: Jesus gave Jezebel time to repent. What does she do with it?

cards.text: So Jesus says He will cast her onto a bed of sickness. And He has a warning for those who commit adultery with her.

cards.question: Those who commit adultery with Jezebel will suffer great tribulation no matter what they do.

cards.text: Then Jesus says He will strike her children dead. And He says all the churches will know something from it.

cards.question: What will all the churches know about Jesus?

cards.text: He also says He will repay each of them according to their deeds. Then He turns to the rest of Thyatira, the ones who don't hold to her teaching and haven't learned the so-called "deep things of Satan".

cards.question: Jesus tells the rest of Thyatira that He'll place more burdens on them.
No further burden for the rest of Thyatira, except one thing. What does Jesus ask of them?

cards.text: Hold fast? Friend, this mustache was BUILT for holding. Now Jesus makes a promise to the one who overcomes and keeps on in His work until the end.

cards.question: Jesus promises the one who overcomes in Thyatira authority over the ___.
The one who overcomes will rule with an iron scepter, just as Jesus received authority from His ___.

cards.text: And one last gift for the one who overcomes: Jesus says He will give him the morning star. Berry would LOVE that one.
Then that line again: "He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches." Four letters down, friend, and Jesus isn't done writing yet.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 5 quotes "My faithful witness Antipas.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Balaam is called 'a prophet' whom Balak 'hired' to curse Israel, but the cited reference (Numbers 22:4-6) never calls Balaam a prophet or says he was hired. Those words come from other verses (2 Peter 2:16 for 'prophet', Deuteronomy 23:4 for 'hired'), which aren't cited. Either cite verses that support the claims or describe Balaam only as Numbers 22:4-6 does: the man Balak, king of Moab, sent for to curse Israel.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The card states that every letter so far has had this line. That is a Bible fact about Revelation 2:7 and 2:11, but it carries no reference for those verses.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The statement says Balaam's teaching misled people 'in Pergamum' into the two sins. Revelation 2:14 says Balaam taught Balak to put a stumbling block before the Israelites. It says only that some in Pergamum hold to that teaching, not that it led Pergamum into those sins. The connection goes beyond what the texts state. Compare the two teachings without saying what Balaam's teaching did in Pergamum.

rule.text: Connecting passages. When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: The right answer depends on both Revelation 2:20 and Revelation 2:14, since the baker has to compare Jezebel's teaching with Balaam's. The card cites only Revelation 2:20.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower. A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: The snooze joke doesn't match the action in the verse. Papa Dorin is given extra time and uses all of it to stall before getting up anyway. Jezebel is given time to repent and is unwilling to repent at all. The joke reads as delaying, not refusing. It also nudges the baker toward the answer on card 6.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'He will repay each of them according to their deeds' narrows the text. Revelation 2:23 says 'I will repay each of you,' right after 'all the churches will know.' Coming right after her children, 'them' reads as Jezebel's followers only. Keep the text's 'each of you' so who is meant stays open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: In stop 2 the choice types strictly alternate: multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice (cards 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 13). Only then do two fill in the blanks come. Cards 1 to 10 also strictly alternate story, choice, story, choice. That reads as a formula.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: Revelation 2:27 says the one who overcomes will rule the nations with an iron scepter 'and shatter them like pottery.' No card tells the 'shatter them like pottery' part, so the baker misses half of the picture in that verse.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
